newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium shortage to boost prices - Bird.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium shortage to boost prices - Bird.

text.p: The aluminium market is likely to remain balanced for the rest of this year, and then tip into deficit next year, providing a boost to prices, industry specialists Anthony Bird and Associates said.
"...we expect prices to move ahead again from the second half of 1997 onwards. Prices should exceed $2,200 in 1998 and could go above $2,800 in 1999," Bird said in its latest quarterly analysis.
Bird said that aluminium consumption has been healthy, and demand is expected to rise more rapidly than industrial production over the next two years.

Supply, meanwhile, has not kept pace with the spurt in demand, and market and producer stocks have fallen. Although new capacity and re-starts will maintain balance this year, strong demand will see a 1998 deficit of some 300,000 tonnes, rising to over 500,000 tonnes the following year.

Smelter capacity growth has been miserably low, although there has been a change in aluminium companies attitude recently. Firms are more interested in expansions and new smelter construction, with a number of announcments expected in coming months.
"But companies have left it very late. We do not think that existing capacity can now be expanded or stretched by enough or quickly enough to avert the coming shortage," Bird said.
